title: Unify session telemetry and introduce compact SDK adapter bridge
author: Lena Park
release_notes: Adds a compact cross-sdk adapter to standardize session telemetry envelopes and reduces SDK surface for streaming handoff; bumps Python/TS/Go SDK versions to align UX. Backwards-compatible; opt-in via feature flag.
description: Summary: This PR introduces a compact adapter layer across the Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs that standardizes session telemetry envelopes, simplifies the streaming handoff surface, and provides a compatibility bridge so existing consumers can opt into the new ergonomics incrementally. Motivation: Multiple internal integrations observed inconsistent session envelope shapes, duplicated telemetry keys, and slightly different retry defaults between SDKs leading to confusion for platform teams and noisy alerting. This was called out in ENG-2143 and tracked as part of cross-SDK parity work in ENG-2199. Goals: (1) standardize the session telemetry payload and sampling keys across SDKs; (2) provide a minimal adapter that consumers can layer over existing session code to get the new semantics with zero downtime; (3) align retry default presets for streaming and token refresh so cross-language clients have comparable behavior; (4) bump SDK minor versions that contain the ergonomic API surface. Changes: - Core: new compact adapter module implemented in each SDK repo (redwood-sdk-python, redwood-sdk-typescript, redwood-sdk-go) and exported from the polyglot 'redwood' root package so examples can import a single compatibility shims path. - Telemetry: unified envelope format: {"session_id","span_id","sampling_rate","client_version","env_tags"} and a lightweight sampler hook. Existing telemetry keys are preserved as aliases for backwards compatibility. - Streaming ergonomics: introduced 'CompactSession.handle' API that wraps existing pullstream/pushstream handles and provides a small set of methods (start, pause, drain, handoff) with clearer lifecycle semantics. - Retry presets: converged streaming retry presets to 'aggressive' (low-latency, limited retries), 'balanced' (default), and 'durable' (longer tail, idempotent workloads). SDKs ship default 'balanced' to avoid changing runtime behavior for most users. - Version bumps: python -> 2.6.0, typescript -> 1.9.0, go -> 1.5.1. - Tests: added cross-sdk unit tests for envelope normalization and an interop smoke test that runs in CI job 'sdk-interop'. Commits: - 7b1c3d1: add compact adapter interface and shared docs - 2aa9d4f: implement telemetry envelope normalization + sampler - e3f8b2a: converge streaming retry presets and add presets test - 5c9f6a4: add TS/Go adapter implementations and examples - a9d2f11: interop smoke test CI job + fixture changes - d1c7b52: docs and examples for migration guide Files changed (high level): - python: redwood_sdk/compact_adapter.py, tests/test_compact_adapter.py, setup.cfg - typescript: packages/sdk/src/compactAdapter.ts, packages/sdk/test/compactAdapter.spec.ts, package.json - go: sdk/compact_adapter.go, sdk/compact_adapter_test.go, go.mod - root redwood: docs/sdk/compact-adapter.md, examples/compact-adapter/* - ci: .github/workflows/sdk-interop.yml Testing & CI: First CI run: lint failures in python (docstring/typing) and a flaky TS unit test. Action: fixed typings and tightened test timing assertions in 2aa9d4f. Reran CI: all checks passed including 'sdk-interop' smoke test on linux-1 and linux-2 runners. Performance: microbenchmarks against the prior streaming surface show median latency unchanged and p50 token processing within 3%; memory overhead from the adapter is negligible for typical session sizes. Review thread (selected): - Samir Gupta (review): "Good shape overall. Please justify the chosen defaults for the retry presets in the PR body and add a short note on why 'balanced' is default." - Lena Park (author): "Added presets rationale to the PR description and unit tests that assert behavior. Balanced chosen to prioritize low-risk migration: ~3 retries with jitter for transient errors, preserves prior median latency in our benchmarks." - Priya Nair (review): "Please add a short migration snippet in docs showing how to opt-in with existing code (hand-off example). Also, add a telemetry alias map so that legacy dashboards can continue to work." - Lena Park: "Added examples/docs and telemetry alias map. Updated release notes accordingly." - Ethan Cole (approve): "Approvals from me after CI green and docs added. Small nit left about one TS naming choice; not blocking." Merge details: - Merge method: squash and merge - Merged by: Priya Nair - Merge commit message: "unify(session+telemetry): compact adapter bridge + sdk bumps" Post-merge actions and TODOs: - Backported minimal compatibility shims to the 2.5.x python branch for a critical partner (follow-up PR tracked in Linear ENG-2261). - Monitor telemetry for increased span_count/alerts for first 48 hours (feature flagging gated rollout). - Follow-up: add migration helper that converts historical telemetry in the ingestion pipeline (ENG-2230). Why this is unique from prior parity work: previous PRs focused on individual SDK surface parity (handshake and backoff semantics). This change is a small-footprint adapter + telemetry unification that lets teams adopt new ergonomics piecemeal without large refactors. It also surfaces an explicit compatibility story (alias map + migration docs) to reduce operational flash.
